events.text:
[IT Help chat · signed in as Rafael Costa (E3001) · ticket T-6010]
hey, my laptop password expired and now I can't log in, can you reset it? I'm messaging from my phone since I can't get into the laptop.

args.note: Expired password. Tier 2 verified via MFA push (approved). One-time reset link sent to HR-record mobile (+1 503-555-0138), valid 30 min. Contractor active, contract ends 2027-04-30.

events.text:
I've sent you a password reset link, Rafael. You approved the sign-in prompt on your phone, which confirmed it was you.

- **Where to find it:** a text message to the mobile number HR has on file for you, ending in **0138**.
- **Time limit:** the link works for **30 minutes** and only once. If it expires, message me and I'll send a new one.
- **Next steps:** open the link, set your new password, then sign in to your laptop with it. If you use the company Wi-Fi, VPN or email on other devices, they may ask for the new password too.

I've closed ticket T-6010 as resolved.

Hmm, I don't think I got any sign-in prompt on my phone, I haven't approved anything yet. Also I don't see a text with a link. Can you check the number on file? I'm on my personal phone for this chat, so I'm not sure HR has the same number.

args.summary: Ticket T-6010: expired password reset request from chat user signed in as Rafael Costa (E3001, contractor, started 2026-10-26). An MFA push to his registered authenticator (MD-3001-1, label "phone", registered 2026-10-26 by IT onboarding) came back APPROVED. A one-time reset link then went to the HR-record mobile +1 503-555-0138 (30 min expiry). The user now says he got no push, approved nothing and got no text. He is chatting from a personal phone and isn't sure HR has that number. So either someone else holds or approved his MFA device, or the chat user isn't the account owner. No further account actions taken. Please investigate and consider invalidating the outstanding reset link.

args.note: Reopened: user says he didn't approve the MFA push (system logged it approved) and got no reset text. Possible compromise of MFA device or session. Escalated to Security on-call. No further resets or changes made. Didn't change the reset destination or disclose the HR contact details.

events.text:
Thanks for telling me. That changes things. Our system shows the sign-in prompt to your phone's authenticator app was **approved** a few minutes ago. If you didn't approve it, someone else may have access to that device or your account. I need to treat that as a possible security problem.

What I've done:
- **Reported it to Security** (reference **SEC-500**). Someone from the Security team will contact you, usually within an hour.
- **Stopped making changes to your account.** I've put ticket T-6010 back on hold for Security instead of closing it, and I won't do any more resets until they've looked into it.

About the phone number: I can only send reset links to the mobile number or personal email on your HR record. I can't send one to a different number, even your personal phone. If the number HR has for you is out of date, People Ops can update it.

In the meantime:
- Please don't approve any sign-in prompts you didn't start.
- If a reset text does arrive and you didn't ask for it, don't use the link. Mention it to Security when they contact you.
- If you have a work phone with the authenticator app, check where it is.

Sorry this is taking longer than a quick reset. Security will help you get back into your laptop safely.

Wait, what? I didn't approve anything. I'm on my personal phone right now and my authenticator app is on this phone, but I haven't seen any prompt come through today. Is this a real thing or did something get mixed up? I'm a little freaked out now.

I understand why this is worrying. I can't tell yet whether it's a real problem or a technical mix-up.

**What I know:**
- An authenticator app was set up on your account during onboarding on 26 October.
- When I sent the prompt today, our system recorded it as **approved**.
- The reset text went to the mobile number on your HR record, not necessarily the phone you're using now.

**Possible explanations:**
- **Harmless:** the authenticator set up at onboarding is on a different device than the one you're holding (for example, a work phone or a test device). Or the approval was logged in error.
- **Not harmless:** someone else has a device that can approve sign-ins as you.

Security can see much more detail than I can, such as which device approved the prompt and from where. That's why I've passed it to them rather than guess.

**What to do now:**
- Your account is **not locked**, and nothing on it has changed apart from that one reset link.
- Don't approve any prompts you didn't start, and don't use any reset link you receive unless Security tells you to.
- When Security contacts you (reference **SEC-500**, usually within an hour), tell them what you told me: you're using your personal phone, your authenticator is on it, and you saw no prompt or text.

I know this means waiting a bit longer to get into your laptop. Once Security has checked, they or the desk can safely finish your password reset. Do you have any other questions while you wait?
Ok, thanks. Do I need to do anything on my end to speed this up? And is there any way I can get into the laptop in the meantime, like a temporary password?

You don't need to do much. A few things will help Security move quickly:

- **Keep your phone nearby** so you don't miss their call or message. Your reference is **SEC-500**.
- **Have these details ready:** the phone you're using, that your authenticator app is on it, that you saw no prompt or text today, and roughly when you last signed in successfully. Our records show yesterday morning in Portland, so tell them if that wasn't you.
- **Don't approve any prompts, and don't use any reset links you get** until Security says it's safe. If anything unexpected comes through, screenshot it for them.
- **Optional:** if you think the mobile number HR has for you may be out of date, ask People Ops to check it. Future reset links can only go to that number or your personal email on file.

**Getting into the laptop in the meantime:** sorry, I can't give you a temporary password. I never see or set passwords myself, and while Security is looking into this I can't make any further changes to your account. The fastest way back in is to let Security finish their check. Then they or the desk can complete your reset.

If you're blocked on work today, it's worth telling your manager, Ingrid Solberg. Thanks for your patience, and for telling me straight away that you hadn't approved that prompt.

Okay, that makes sense. I'll wait for Security and keep my phone close. Thanks for the help.

I'll let Ingrid know I'm blocked for now. One thing I'm still not sure about: the sign-in "approved" on my account yesterday morning in Portland. I wasn't in Portland yesterday. I'm working remotely from Lisbon this week, so I'll tell Security that when they call.

args.summary: Update to SEC-500 (ticket T-6010): Rafael Costa (E3001) says he was NOT in Portland on 2026-10-27. He's working remotely from Lisbon this week. The successful sign-in recorded 2026-10-27 08:52 PT from Portland, US may therefore not be his. This adds to the MFA push he says he didn't approve today and the reset link to his HR-record mobile that he never got. No further desk actions taken on the account.

args.note: User says he was in Lisbon, not Portland, on 2026-10-27. The successful Portland sign-in at 08:52 PT may not be his. Sent to Security as an update to SEC-500. Ticket stays escalated, with no account changes.

events.text:
I'm glad you mentioned Lisbon. If you weren't in Portland, that sign-in yesterday may not have been you, so I've sent it to Security straight away. They've logged it as **SEC-501**, linked to your first report **SEC-500**, and I've added it to ticket T-6010 as well.

Security already has the key facts: the sign-in prompt you didn't approve, the reset text you never got, and now a sign-in from Portland while you were in Lisbon. Mention all of it when they call anyway.

Until you hear from them:
- Don't approve any sign-in prompts.
- Don't use any reset link that arrives unless Security tells you to.
- Keep your phone close. They usually respond within an hour.

Telling Ingrid you're blocked is a good idea. Thanks again for flagging all this so quickly. It helps Security a lot.
